newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Rwanda wants U.N. Zaire force mandate changed.
newsitem.headline: Rwanda wants U.N. Zaire force mandate changed.

text.p: Rwanda's U.N. envoy said on Friday the mandate of the planned United Nations multinational force to Zaire was now irrelevant and resources should be directed instead to Rwanda.
Envoy Gideon Kayianamura said he had asked the U.N. Security Council president and others involved "to rethink the mandate and the relevance of this multinational force in the circumstances."

Kayianamura's comments came at a news conference after the United Nations said that although 400,000 Rwandan refugees were heading home from eastern Zaire, a multinational force was still badly needed to help provide aid and logistics.
U.N. spokesman Sylvana Foa told Reuters: "Everybody is absolutely elated, but we still desperately need the multinational force."

"We have stocks in Rwanda for about 450,000 people, but we are going to need a lot of help to move these people around," she said, adding that only a military operation could provide the required logistics.
